terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
evidence: Cic. Att. 5.11.1: hui, totiēnsne mē litterās dedisse Rōmam, cum ad tē nūllās darem?
Ter. Ph. 663–664: Oi! hui! Nimium est.
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “astonishment or admiration”. Often with quam or a question; in Cicero’s letters it marks his own surprise at himself (hui, quam diū dē nūgīs!). For open-mouthed wonder, papae (see wow!).

phrases.latin: hui, totiēnsne mē litterās dedisse Rōmam, cum ad tē nūllās darem?
phrases.english: Well, well: have I sent letters to Rome so often without sending you any?
Goodness, how long I’ve gone on about trifles!

sources: Lewis & Short: hui · Lewis & Short: papae
